results.question: Which rice diseases have an identified causal pathogen?
results.rationale: Aetiological completeness. A disease without a causal agent cannot support any downstream causal query.

results.question: Which diseases and pests have at least one observable symptom?
results.rationale: Diagnosability. Without a symptom link an entity is invisible to field-observation-driven inference.

results.question: Which diseases and pests have at least one control treatment?
results.rationale: Actionability. The KG must not diagnose what it cannot advise on.

results.question: Which symptoms are attached to at least one disease or pest?
results.rationale: Detects orphan symptoms - vocabulary declared but never used in a diagnostic pattern.

results.question: For which diseases/pests can we state both the growth stage of occurrence and an environmental factor raising their risk?
results.rationale: Multi-criteria contextualisation. Both joins are mandatory (no OPTIONAL), so the CQ measures real co-population of occursIn and increaseRiskOf.

results.question: Which growth stages have a documented vulnerability profile naming a concrete disease or pest?
results.rationale: vulnerableTo is the most frequently asserted domain relation in the KG (59 triples), so it must be exercised directly.

results.question: Is the stage-vulnerability view consistent with the occurrence view (vulnerableTo without a matching occursIn)?
results.rationale: Integrity constraint. If stage G is vulnerableTo entity E, then E should occursIn G. Any row is an inconsistency.

results.question: Which preventive treatments carry an explicit growth-stage prerequisite for their application?
results.rationale: Prevention advice without a timing constraint is not operationalisable in the field.

results.question: For which declared insect vectors is the transmission chain vector -> pathogen -> disease fully traversable?
results.rationale: The canonical multi-hop epidemiological query. The denominator is the set of pests asserted to transmit something (not all pests), so the measure is chain completeness, not vector prevalence.

results.question: Are there insect vectors for which no control treatment is recorded, leaving the transmission chain unbreakable?
results.rationale: A vector chain that cannot be interrupted has no advisory value. Splitting this from CQ-09 separates 'the chain exists' from 'the chain is actionable'.

results.question: For which diseases is the full risk-to-remedy chain traversable: environmental factor -> disease -> symptom -> treatment?
results.rationale: End-to-end decision-support path. This is the query an advisory application actually needs to answer.

results.question: For which diseases and pests does the KG reach the management layer, i.e. recommend a concrete ManagementAction?
results.rationale: Tests that diagnosis terminates in an operational decision. Note the direction of rice:recommends in this KG is entity -> action, not action -> treatment.

results.question: Does every severity level map to a recommended management action, so that triage advice is total?
results.rationale: Severity-driven triage is the decision layer of the KG. A severity level with no action is a hole in the advisory logic.

results.question: Which observations are SymptomaticObservations, i.e. members of the defined class 'Observation that captures some Symptom'?
results.rationale: The one genuine defined class in the ontology. Asserted membership is zero by construction; a non-zero entailed count proves the OWL axiomatisation does work SPARQL alone cannot.

results.question: Can the KG be queried in the inverse direction, e.g. disease -> causedBy -> pathogen and symptom -> indicates -> disease?
results.rationale: 14 of 26 object properties are declared as owl:inverseOf but never asserted. Query robustness depends on materialising them.

results.question: Which image observations can be grounded all the way to an agronomic recommendation: image -> annotated class -> symptom and treatment?
results.rationale: The central multimodal claim of the KG. The denominator is restricted to images annotated with a Disease or Pest: images labelled with a HealthStatus (healthy plants) correctly have no symptom or treatment, and including them would understate grounding by a fixed 17%.

results.question: Which annotated classes of the image corpus are typed as a domain entity (Disease, Pest or HealthStatus)?
results.rationale: Checks that dataset labels were reconciled with the ontology rather than left as free-floating individuals.

results.question: Which symptoms are grounded in visual evidence, i.e. captured by at least one image observation?
results.rationale: Symptom-level visual grounding is what distinguishes an MMKG from a text ontology with images bolted on. Expected to expose the sharpest gap in the current release.

results.question: Are there image observations lacking a content URL or a source dataset provenance link?
results.rationale: Integrity constraint on the media layer. Any row means an image cannot be retrieved or attributed.

results.question: How many sensor observations does the KG contain?
results.rationale: Declared extension point. Recorded as a measurement, not scored, so the roadmap gap stays visible without inflating or deflating the pass rate.

results.question: Which reified domain assertions carry both an authoritative source URI and a bibliographic citation?
results.rationale: Provenance completeness - the scientific-defensibility claim of the KG.

results.question: Are there domain assertions with missing or incomplete provenance - either no reified axiom at all, or an axiom missing its source, citation or evidence type?
results.rationale: Integrity constraint complementing CQ-21. Extended on 2026-09-14: the original form checked only axioms that exist, so an assertion with no axiom at all was invisible to both CQ-21 and CQ-22, and v0.6 carried two such assertions while both reported full provenance. Runs on the asserted graph, since materialised inverses are never reified and would all count as violations. Extended again on 2026-09-23: rice:hasPathogenGroup joined the list - a property left out of it is invisible to this check, which is the failure mode the 2026-09-14 extension was written for. Extended again on 2026-09-17: ResistanceAssessment individuals carry their provenance on the individual itself rather than on an axiom, so an assessment missing its source, citation or evidence type is reported too.

results.question: Which biological entities (disease, pathogen, pest) are aligned to an external vocabulary (EPPO, AGROVOC or NCBI Taxonomy)?
results.rationale: Interoperability. Written as a coverage measure rather than an OPTIONAL projection, which would report success even when every alignment column is null.

results.question: Are annotation literals lexically consistent, i.e. is rice:evidenceType uniformly language-tagged?
results.rationale: Literal-hygiene constraint. An untagged duplicate of a tagged value silently splits GROUP BY and breaks lang() filters.

results.question: Under entailment, is any individual typed as both a Symptom and a Disease?
results.rationale: Category discipline. Symptom and Disease are intended to be disjoint; an overlap means either a mistyped individual or a property domain that is declared too narrowly. This constraint is checked on the materialised graph, because the conflict is produced by inference and is invisible in the asserted triples.
